correctness.rationale: The gap lemma reduces the all-factor attractor assertion to factors of unselected intervals. The three constructive cases are exhaustive and their anchors cover each pure and mixed gap factor. In the sole three-point regime, three uniquely occurring factors have disjoint intervals, so no pair works. One point cannot hit both one-letter factors. Parameter substitution proves the rational enumerator; the order-three pole at z=1 and lower-order other poles yield the 1/3 coefficient ratio. verify_exhaustive.py and verify_independent.py were executed from this package and agree in the stated finite ranges; the proof establishes the unbounded theorem.

value.rationale: An exact minimum-factor-attractor classification for a natural palindromic five-run family resolves a nontrivial gap beyond previously classified three- and four-run families. The transition occurs in a positive-density one-third subfamily and is supported by structural non-overlapping unique-factor obstructions and explicit optimal positions, not a small arbitrary table. Its rational count and density permit combinatorial comparison of repetitiveness regimes without claiming an unrelated broad theorem.
